intro.title: Your training at a glance
intro.body: This page shows the courses you **must** take, what is due, and the certificates you hold. The requirements come from the organisation's assignment rules (for your department, job position or as a new hire) and from training assigned to you directly.
steps: Start with anything marked **Overdue** or **Expired**.
Open a course, go through the lessons and finish the last step.
Your training record and certificate are created automatically when you finish.

why.body: Every ISO management system standard requires the organisation to make sure people are **competent** for their work and **aware** of the policy, their contribution and the consequences of not following the system. The EU AI Act also requires AI literacy for staff who use AI systems.

empty.title: No training required right now
empty.body: When a course is assigned to you, or a rule makes it required for your role or department, it appears here with its due date. You can also browse the course catalogue and take any published course on your own.

intro.title: The course catalogue
intro.body: A course teaches people what they need to know and documents that they learned it. It can be an **online course** with lessons and a quiz, a **read-and-understood** confirmation of a controlled document, or **external training** recorded by a training manager.
steps: Filter by category, type or status, and save the filters as a view.
Open a course to see its lessons, who must take it and who has completed it.
New courses start as drafts and become available when they are published.

why.body: A catalogue of approved courses makes awareness training repeatable and measurable instead of a one-off presentation. Information security and privacy awareness are explicit requirements.

empty.title: No courses yet
empty.body: Start with the training everyone needs: an onboarding course, information security awareness or the quality policy. You can draft a course from an existing procedure in a few minutes.

intro.title: Working with a course
intro.body: A course goes from **draft** to **published** and finally **archived**. Changing the content of a published course creates a new **version**, and the revisions show who changed what and why.
steps: Add rules so the right people get the course automatically. You see who a rule assigns before you save it.
Use **Assign** for individuals, for example after an incident.
The requirements the course documents are shown in the panel on the right, so auditors find the evidence.

why.body: Auditors check that competence needs are defined, that training was given, and that its effectiveness was evaluated. A course with rules, records and evaluations covers all three.

rules.help: A rule says who must take the course and how many days they get. Choose a department or job position for the job people do; an access role only covers rights in CoreFlow. Renewals are assigned automatically before a certificate expires.
rules.example: Job position: Warehouse operative, 30 days. New hires, 14 days.

effectiveness.help: Did the training work? Compare with the course's effectiveness criteria, using observation, key figures or audits, not only quiz scores.
effectiveness.example: Effective: deviations of this kind halved after the course.

intro.title: Building a good course
intro.body: Keep lessons short and practical: one topic per lesson, a few minutes each, with examples from everyday work. Use the quiz to check that people understood what matters most.
steps: Choose the type: online course, read and understood, or external training.
Write the learning objectives: what participants can do afterwards.
Add two to four quiz questions per lesson if you need proof of understanding.
Under **Requirements and validity**, choose how long the course is valid, which requirements it documents and which competence it gives.

why.body: Training only builds competence when it is relevant and checked. A defined pass mark and validity period make the result objective and repeatable.

description.help: What the course covers and who it is for. Learners see this before they start.
description.example: How to report and handle information security incidents. For all employees.

kind.help: An online course has lessons and quizzes. Read and understood asks the learner to confirm a controlled document. External training is held elsewhere and recorded by a training manager.

document.help: The controlled document the course is about. Required for read and understood: the confirmation is stored against the document's current approved revision.

passMark.help: The share of quiz answers that must be correct to pass. 80 % is common; use 100 % for safety-critical rules. Only applies to online courses with a quiz.

validity.help: How long a completion stays valid. Leave empty if the training never expires. Renewals are assigned automatically before expiry.

lessonBody.help: Write in short paragraphs. A line that starts with ## becomes a new step in the lesson; short bullet lists work best.
lessonBody.example:
## What is an incident?
Any event that could harm the confidentiality, integrity or availability of information.

owner.help: The person responsible for the course. Their name appears as the issuer on the certificate.

learningObjectives.help: What participants can do after the course, one objective per line. They are shown before the course starts and printed on the certificate.
learningObjectives.example: Report an information security incident within one hour.

clauseRefs.help: The requirements in the standards that this course helps the organisation meet. They become confirmed links, so the course counts as evidence for the requirement.
clauseRefs.example: ISO 27001 · A.6.3 for an information security awareness course

competences.help: The competence from People that someone gets when they pass the course. It is renewed on the employee's profile, and a higher level is never lowered.

effectivenessCriteria.help: What shows that the training worked. Use the criteria when you evaluate the course after a while.
effectivenessCriteria.example: No repeat deviations of this kind for six months.

intro.title: How this course works
intro.body: Work through the lessons in order. Your progress is saved as you go, so you can stop and continue later. Finish with the final step to get your completion record.
steps: Read each lesson step and open any linked video or document.
Answer the final quiz. You can try again if you do not reach the pass mark.
Give feedback so the course can be improved.

intro.title: The final step
intro.body: Answer every question, then submit. Your answers are scored by the system and a completion record with a certificate number is created when you pass.

intro.title: Who takes which course
intro.body: An assignment asks one person to complete one course by a due date. Assignments come from rules, new-hire [[onboarding|onboarding]], renewals before expiry, a new revision of a document, or someone assigning the course directly.
steps: Choose **Overdue** to follow up missed due dates.
Tick several assignments to send a reminder, move the due date or cancel them together.
Group by course or person to see who is missing what.

why.body: Planning who needs which training, and following up, is how you show that competence is ensured and not left to chance.

empty.title: No assignments
empty.body: Assignments appear when a course is assigned to you or when an assignment rule includes you. Browse the catalogue to find training you can take now.

intro.title: One assignment
intro.body: The assignment closes automatically when the person completes the course. Training managers can send a reminder, change the due date or cancel the assignment if it no longer applies.

why.body: Assignments with due dates and their history show that training needs were planned and followed up.

dueDate.help: When the training must be completed. Reminders are sent before the date and the assignment shows as overdue afterwards.

intro.title: Evidence of competence
intro.body: A training record shows that a person completed a course: when, which version, the result and how long it is valid. Online courses are recorded automatically; external and classroom training is recorded by a training manager.
steps: Choose **Expiring within 30 days** to plan renewals.
Choose **Missing documentation** to find external training without an attached certificate.
Export the list as CSV when an auditor asks for evidence.

why.body: The standards require the organisation to **retain documented information as evidence of competence**. These records are that evidence.

empty.title: No training records yet
empty.body: Records are created when someone passes a course or when a training manager records external training. Complete your first course to get your first certificate.

expires.help: When the training stops being valid. Leave empty to use the course's validity period, or if it never expires.

provider.help: The supplier that delivered the training. The record is then linked to the supplier, and you see the training from there.

intro.title: A completion record
intro.body: This record is the evidence that the training took place. The certificate can be printed, and the learner's feedback and the effectiveness evaluation show whether the training worked.

why.body: Where applicable, the organisation must take actions to acquire competence and **evaluate the effectiveness** of the actions taken.

effectiveness.help: Did the training achieve its goal for this person? Base it on observed behaviour, results or follow-up, not only on the quiz score.
effectiveness.example: Effective: incident reports after the course are complete and on time.

intro.title: The training matrix
intro.body: The matrix shows every person against every course with the status of what is required. The percentage at the top is the share of required training in place, and each course has its own percentage.
steps: Filter by category, department or job position to focus on one area.
Click a cell to open the record or assignment behind it, or a name for the person's training profile.
Print or export the matrix for [[management-review|management review]] and audits.

why.body: A competence or training matrix is the most common way to show auditors that needs are known and met across the organisation.

intro.title: Assign training
intro.body: Choose a published course, the people who must take it and a due date. Use rules on the course when it applies to a whole department or job position, so new people get it automatically.

course.help: Only published courses can be assigned. If you came from a deviation, choose the course that closes the competence gap.

intro.title: The training plan
intro.body: The plan shows month by month when training is due and when certificates expire. It is built from the assignments and rules, including rules that repeat every year.
steps: Start with what is already overdue.
Move 12 months forward or back to see the yearly programme.
Print the plan when an auditor asks for the training plan.

why.body: The standards require the organisation to plan how it gets the competence it needs and keeps it up to date. A plan with dates shows that this is not left to chance.

sections.heading: Competence and awareness
sections.body: **Competence** is the ability to apply knowledge and skills to get the intended result. **Awareness** means people know the policy, how they contribute and what happens if they do not follow the system. Both are required by every ISO management system standard (clauses 7.2 and 7.3).

sections.heading: From need to evidence
sections.body:
1. Decide what competence each role needs.
2. Close gaps with training, mentoring or hiring.
3. **Keep records** that show the competence is in place.
4. Check that the action actually worked.

sections.heading: How CoreFlow helps
sections.body: Assignment rules give the right courses to the right people, renewals are assigned automatically before certificates expire, and every completion becomes a record with a certificate number and the course version.

quiz.question: What do the standards require you to keep as evidence of competence?
options: Nothing, a verbal confirmation is enough
Documented information, such as training records
quiz.explanation: Clause 7.2 requires documented information as evidence of competence.

quiz.question: What should you do after training has been given?
quiz.explanation: The organisation must evaluate the effectiveness of the actions taken.

sections.heading: Why evaluate
sections.body: A passed quiz shows that someone understood the content on the day. Effectiveness asks a different question: **did the training change how the work is done?**

sections.heading: How to evaluate
sections.body:
- Look at results: fewer errors, complete reports, passed inspections.
- Observe the work or ask the manager after a few weeks.
- Use learner feedback to improve the course itself.

quiz.question: Which is the best evidence that training was effective?

home.title: The course catalogue
home.body: Browse every published course, including the ones you do not have to take.

home.title: Programme figures
home.body: If you follow up training, you see how much required training is in place, open and overdue assignments, and certificates expiring soon.

courses.title: Create a course
courses.body: Start from scratch or let the assistant draft lessons and quizzes from a procedure or a topic. Courses start as drafts.

matrix.title: Narrow the matrix
matrix.body: Filter by category, department or job position to see one area at a time.

matrix.title: Required training in place
matrix.body: The share of required training that is in place. Use it in management review.
